subject.title: refactor(protocol): pre-publish cheat-window cleanup and vintage tracking

question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed hard-breaking cleanup of the asserted unshipped and beta-only gateway-protocol surfaces before `@openclaw/gateway-protocol` is published as public npm API?
rationale: The branch deliberately removes and renames protocol contracts rather than preserving a migration layer; source review can assess implementation coherence, but only maintainers can accept the stated release and external-consumer boundary.

options.title: Approve the compatibility window
options.body: Confirm that the shipped-surface audit is sufficient and accept the renamed and removed protocol contracts before public npm publication.

options.title: Preserve a transition path
options.body: Keep the existing public fields or exports with a documented deprecation and remove them only after an announced migration window.

options.title: Split publication preparation
options.body: Land non-breaking metadata and dead-code cleanup separately, then revisit destructive protocol changes with an explicit release plan.

recommendation.title: Approve the compatibility window
recommendation.body: Confirm that the shipped-surface audit is sufficient and accept the renamed and removed protocol contracts before public npm publication.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored and is assigned to the protocol cleanup, so they are the closest available routing candidate for documenting the compatibility audit and seeking the final owner decision.
